title: The $200 Million Wall Painting Deal

beats.say: In 2005, an artist was offered $60,000 cash or company stock for painting startup walls, and chose the stock.
beats.visual: Extreme low angle shot of a massive concrete building edge cutting against a stormy blue hour sky.

beats.say: That single decision on a paint job set off a chain reaction worth hundreds of millions.
beats.visual: Extreme close up of rough grey concrete wet with rain under a single cold sodium light.

beats.say: Most people take the immediate cash payout because it feels safe, tangible, and secure right now.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a lone person walking away down a dark, fog-cut highway at night.

beats.say: You think cash in hand is always the smart play, but ownership beats labor every single time.
beats.visual: High angle shot of empty wet asphalt reflecting harsh cold fluorescent parking lot lights.

beats.say: The startup was Facebook, and the artist was David Choe, hired to paint the walls of their first office.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a massive dark industrial bridge underpass with water below.

beats.say: Why would anyone gamble $60,000 guaranteed on a risky internet project nobody knew yet?
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a towering steel structure disappearing into thick grey fog.

beats.say: He bet on the leverage of equity over a flat hourly or project rate.
beats.visual: Close up of rough weathered timber beams under a single practical overhead light.

beats.say: That gamble turned into stock worth about $200 million when the company went public years later.
beats.visual: Extreme close up of dark open water rippling under cold sodium street lamps.

beats.say: Choosing equity over cash traded immediate spending power for a massive future ownership stake.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a single figure standing on a vast concrete ridge line at dusk.

beats.say: That's how real wealth gets built from a single ordinary workday.
beats.visual: Wide shot of a dark empty city street cutting through tall towers in blue hour.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Extreme low angle looking up a towering concrete pillar into a heavy rainstorm.

caption: Choosing ownership over a paycheck built a $200 million fortune from a single paint job. #money #wealth #investing #finance #history
description: In 2005, artist David Choe took stock instead of cash for painting Facebook's first office. That single choice created a $200 million fortune through equity.
